item.title: Pointed Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory
item.author: Andrei Bud, Richard Haburcak
item.description:
Andrei Bud, Richard Haburcak

Matched: Andrei Bud · math.AG · new

We study the geometry of Hurwitz--Brill--Noether spaces with vanishing conditions at a totally ramified point. Degeneration to a curve with an elliptic tail simplifies the combinatorics of Larson, Larson--Larson--Vogt, and Aggarwal, giving inductive proofs of Aggarwal's results in the one-point setting, and yields an efficient recursion for the algebraic Euler characteristics. Finally, when the expected dimension is negative, we give a numerical criterion ensuring the universal Hurwitz--Brill--Noether locus admits a component of expected relative dimension, generically finite over its image in the Hurwitz space, analogous to the existing results of Pflueger and Teixidor i Bigas for classical Brill--Noether loci.

item.title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
item.author: Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan
item.description:
Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.AG · new

We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang's descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, K\"ahler--Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture.

item.title: The inverse local-relative correspondence and the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation
item.author: Jianjun Fu, Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang
item.description:
Jianjun Fu, Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang

Matched: Shuai Guo · math.AG · new

We prove the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation for the local Gromov--Witten theory of smooth weak del Pezzo surfaces, by identifying its unique formal solution with the inverse of the local-relative correspondence. We construct this inverse through an associative set-partition convolution and establish the identification using Zagier's recursion for the Bloch--Okounkov $n$-point function. The proof applies in all genera and includes non-toric surfaces.

item.title: Balancing tautological intersection numbers
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.AG, hep-th · cross

We prove the three balancing inequalities conjectured by the authors about 20 years ago: moving one unit from a larger index to a smaller one cannot decrease a mixed tautological intersection number, whether the two distinguished insertions are psi classes, kappa classes, or Hodge Chern classes.

item.title: Uniform asymptotics and the Weil--Petersson constant
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.AG · new

In their celebrated work on the large-genus asymptotic expansion of Weil--Petersson volumes, Mirzakhani and Zograf left open the question of whether the Weil--Petersson constant satisfies $C_{\mathrm{WP}}=\pi^{-1/2}$. We resolve the conjecture affirmatively. Our strategy is to consider a family of spectral curves interpolating between $y=z-4z^3$ and $y=\sin(2\pi z)/(2\pi)$. For each fixed number $n\geq2$ of marked points, we normalize the cusp coefficients using the action integral and the derivative at its first positive zero. We prove that the logarithmic derivatives of these normalized coefficients with respect to the family parameter are $O_n(g^{-1})$, uniformly along the family. The proof combines the descendant recursion, positivity, the dilaton equation, KdV, and coefficient asymptotics for the Painlev\'e I equation.

item.title: From one particle to N particles: uniform transport-information and log-Sobolev inequalities for Coulomb gases on the torus
item.author: A Guillin (LMBP), W Liu (LMBP), B Nectoux (LMBP), L Wu (LMBP)
item.description:
A Guillin (LMBP), W Liu (LMBP), B Nectoux (LMBP), L Wu (LMBP)

Matched: Longting Wu · math.FA, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We study how a functional inequality satisfied by the one-particle conditional distributions of a Gibbs measure, with a constant independent of the positions of the other particles, can be propagated to the whole N -particle system, with a constant independent of N , when the interaction is singular. Our model is the Coulomb gas on the torus T 3 in the mean-field regime. We distinguish two mechanisms. The first one is a dependent tensorization, governed by Dobrushin-Wu interdependence coefficients. It yields uniform Poincar{\'e} and transport-information W 2 I inequalities with fully explicit constants. We explain why this mechanism does not extend to the log-Sobolev inequality: the Zegarlinski-type coefficients, which require pointwise bounds on the interaction, are infinite. The second mechanism is a tensorization with a defect. Using a uniform bound on the partition function due to Duerinckx and Jabin, it yields a uniform log-Sobolev inequality for the Coulomb gas on T 3 at small charge. We identify the assumptions on the interaction under which each mechanism applies. All the results are then extended to the two-dimensional Coulomb gas and to periodic Riesz gases 1/|x|^s , 0 < s $\le$ 1. The extension to d $\ge$ 4 is also discussed.

item.title: MONODROMY AND BIG QUANTUM COHOMOLOGY OF HYPERPLANE SECTIONS OF (CO)ADJOINT VARIETIES
item.author: Vladimiro Benedetti (LJAD), Simone Billi (CMLS), Nicolas Perrin (CMLS)
item.description:
Vladimiro Benedetti (LJAD), Simone Billi (CMLS), Nicolas Perrin (CMLS)

Matched: Nicolas Perrin · math.AG · new

We study the monodromy representation of general hyperplane sections of (co)adjoint varieties. We apply this result to reduce the generic semisemplicity of the big quantum cohomology to its ambient part, and to prove that the big quantum cohomology of general hyperplane sections of IGr(2, 6) is generically semisimple and satisfies Dubrovin's conjecture.

item.title: Deligne--Faltings Logarithmic Derived Geometry with a View towards Logarithmic GLSM
item.author: Felix Janda, Ruoxi Li
item.description:
Felix Janda, Ruoxi Li

Matched: Felix Janda · math.AG · new

Many perfect obstruction theories and virtual cycles in enumerative geometry are shadows from derived geometry. In this paper, we give a general construction of reduced perfect obstruction theories arising from a geometric reduction of the derived stack $X$ with respect to a $(-1)$-shifted log function $w_\alpha$. Notably, this construction leads to a decomposition of the virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ into the reduced virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{red}}$ and a reduced boundary cycle $[\Delta_X]^\red$. Our construction is motivated by future applications to the moduli stack of UMD logarithmic R-maps in log GLSM \cite{CJR21}. Along the way, we develop logarithmic analogs of several constructions in derived geometry, in particular proving a logarithmic Lagrangian intersection theorem.

item.title: The fifteenth cohomology group of moduli spaces of stable curves
item.author: Amy Bradford, Aitor Iribar L\'opez, Andreas Kretschmer, Hannah Larson
item.description:
Amy Bradford, Aitor Iribar L\'opez, Andreas Kretschmer, Hannah Larson

Matched: Hannah Larson · math.AG · new

The new framework of semi-tautological extensions has allowed for explicit understanding of low-degree odd cohomology groups of moduli spaces of stable curves. Let $S^*_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) \subset H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ denote the semi-tautological extension generated by $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$, that is, the smallest system of subrings of $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ containing $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$ and the tautological subrings, which is also closed under pullbacks along forgetful maps and pushforwards along gluing maps. Recently, it has been shown that $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{11}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ and $H^{13}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{13}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g$ and $n$. Meanwhile, $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}) \neq S_\omega^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n})$ for all $n \geq 15$. Nevertheless, we prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}) = S^{15}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for all $n$. Moreover, we determine all relations in $S_\omega^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g \geq 2$ and give explicit bases for this vector space in terms of decorated graphs. Conditional upon the conjectured dimension of $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,14})$, we also prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n}) = S^{15}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n})$ for all $n$. As an application, we prove $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = RH^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for several new small pairs $(g,n)$.

item.title: On Chow and Picard groups of Richardson varieties
item.author: David Anderson, Sam Payne
item.description:
David Anderson, Sam Payne

Matched: Sam Payne · math.AG · new

We show that if $\Pi \subseteq G/P$ is a projected Richardson variety, then the degree map $\mathrm{Pic}(\Pi) \to A_1(\Pi)^\vee$ is injective. Moreover, it is an isomorphism in characteristic zero and in all but finitely many positive characteristics. We conjecture that it is an isomorphism in every characteristic. Our proofs are geometric, using a linear paving, topological properties of klt singularities, and reduction to characteristic zero.

item.title: Sharp parameter gaps for quantized Mabuchi energies and cscK metrics
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Liangdi Zhang
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Liangdi Zhang

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.DG · new

For polarized manifolds, we show that semistability for the quantized Mabuchi energy at one fixed finite parameter is equivalent to uniform K-stability and to unique existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler (cscK) metrics. We obtain sharp comparisons between quantized Mabuchi slopes at different parameters and with the ordinary Mabuchi slope. In the presence of automorphisms, we give an equivariant criterion using torus twists under the vanishing of the Futaki character. The estimates also hold for finite-energy geodesic rays in compact K\"ahler classes. On a fixed ruled surface with discrete automorphism group, we construct cscK polarizations with unbounded critical parameters. Their ratios to the $\alpha$-invariant are also unbounded.

item.title: Universality of $\mathsf{CohFT}$ of $\mathsf{Hilb}_n(S)$
item.author: Denis Nesterov, Hsian-Hua Tseng
item.description:
Denis Nesterov, Hsian-Hua Tseng

Matched: Denis Nesterov, Hsian-Hua Tseng · math.AG · new

By virtue of their relation to Fulton--MacPherson compactifications, the cohomological field theory of Hilbert schemes of points on a surface, in extremal curve classes, is universally and effectively determined by the characteristic numbers of the surface and by the corresponding theory of Hilbert schemes of the affine plane. As a consequence, we compute the extremal genus 1 Gromov--Witten invariants of Hilbert schemes of all surfaces.

item.title: The moduli space of curves of genus 16 is uniruled
item.author: Gavril Farkas, Alessandro Verra
item.description:
Gavril Farkas, Alessandro Verra

Matched: Gavril Farkas · math.AG · new

Using in a novel way non-abelian Brill-Noether theory, we show that the moduli space of curves of genus 16 is uniruled. This is the highest genus for which such a result is known.

PDF

item.title: Motivic Euler characteristics of moduli spaces of curves
item.author: Jonas Bergstr\"om, Samir Canning, Dan Petersen, Johannes Schmitt
item.description:
Jonas Bergstr\"om, Samir Canning, Dan Petersen, Johannes Schmitt

Matched: Johannes Schmitt, Samir Canning · math.AG · new

A combination of recent results of Canning--Larson--Payne--Willwacher and Payne--Willwacher is that the motivic Euler characteristic of the moduli space $M_{g,n}$ of nonsingular curves with $n$ markings is polynomial in the Tate motive if and only if $g=0$ or $3g+2n<25$. In the cases when $g\geq 1$ and $3g+2n<25$, there are $32$ pairs $(g,n)$ where the motivic Euler characteristic has been computed. We compute the motivic Euler characteristic for $9$ more pairs, leaving only $6$ pairs where the motivic Euler characteristic is polynomial but unknown. In genus $4$, we moreover compute the answer when $n=7$, i.e.~the first non-polynomial case.

item.title: Transverse rational curves and the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture
item.author: Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan
item.description:
Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.AG · new

We prove that every compact connected positive quaternionic--K\"ahler manifold of real dimension $4n$ with $n\ge2$ is isometric to a Wolf space after rescaling the metric by a positive constant. This proves the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. The proof uses transverse rational curves and the contact structure of the twistor space.

item.title: The Prym-Green conjecture in even genera up to 30
item.author: Sam Payne, Thomas Willwacher
item.description:
Sam Payne, Thomas Willwacher

Matched: Sam Payne · math.AG · new

We prove the Prym-Green conjecture in every even genus from 20 to 30. The genus 24 case disproves the suggestion of Chiodo-Eisenbud-Farkas-Schreyer that the conjecture might fail in every genus divisible by 8. Our proof uses rational nodal curves with cyclic symmetry to decompose the relevant Koszul differential into a direct sum of smaller maps indexed by characters. We carry out the resulting rank computations over finite fields using the block Wiedemann algorithm.

item.title: Suciu's Conjecture on hyperplane arrangements
item.author: Marian Aprodu, Gavril Farkas, Claudiu Raicu, Alexander I. Suciu
item.description:
Marian Aprodu, Gavril Farkas, Claudiu Raicu, Alexander I. Suciu

Matched: Gavril Farkas · math.AG, math.CO · cross

We prove that the resonance of any hyperplane arrangement is separable. Using the main result from arXiv:2512.10160 this proves Suciu's conjecture on the fundamental group of every hyperplane arrangement, in its most effective form.

item.title: Quantum cohomology, Hitchin systems, and Fourier--Mukai comparison
item.author: Yunfeng Jiang, Hsian-Hua Tseng
item.description:
Yunfeng Jiang, Hsian-Hua Tseng

Matched: Hsian-Hua Tseng · math.AG · new

Let $X$ be the moduli space of stable trace-free rank $r$ Higgs bundles over a smooth projective curve $C$ with fixed determinant $\Lambda\in\Pic(C)$ and $\gcd(r,\deg\Lambda)=1$. We prove that the $\cc^*$-equivariant quantum product of a divisor on $X$ is given by the Steinberg correspondence of the Lagrangian Steinberg cycle in $X\times X$. The Steinberg cycle is the image of the reduced virtual fundamental cycle of the $2$-pointed Kontsevich stable map space to $X$ under evaluation map. For $\Gamma=\Pic^0(C)[r]$, we give a character decomposition for $\Gamma$-invariant curve classes or finite orbit sums. In rank two and genus two we explicitly determine its fifteen endoscopic lines and the reduced spectral discriminant. %The resulting endoscopic support statement is cohomological, not a determination of the entire Chow cycle. For $\widehat X=[X/\Gamma]$, which is the moduli space of stable $\PGL_r$-Higgs bundles over $C$. We consider the orbifold quantum cohomology theory from a gerbe-twisted theory. The complex K-theory $\KU^*(X)$ and twisted K-theory $\KU^*([X/\Gamma],\alpha)$ by the lifting $\mu_r$-gerbe $\alpha$ of the universal projective bundle is an isomorphism, and is given by the Fourier-Mukai transformation. We prove that the Fourier-Mukai transformation is compatible with the quantum product by the divisors.

item.title: Intrinsic mirror symmetry for orbifold cubic surfaces and the $A_1$ spherical DAHA
item.author: Pierrick Bousseau, Sayan Chattopadhyay
item.description:
Pierrick Bousseau, Sayan Chattopadhyay

Matched: Pierrick Bousseau · math.AG, hep-th, math.GT · cross

We determine the intrinsic mirror of an orbifold cubic surface with three nodes and interpret the resulting geometry through mirror symmetry between the $PGL(2,\mathbb{C})$ and $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ character varieties of the once-punctured torus. We further construct a quantization of the mirror using higher genus Gromov-Witten theory and show that it recovers the $A_1$ spherical double affine Hecke algebra.

item.title: Structure of higher-genus open-closed Gromov--Witten theory of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(p-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-p-1)$
item.author: Shuai Guo, Jingyi Xu, Qingsheng Zhang
item.description:
Shuai Guo, Jingyi Xu, Qingsheng Zhang

Matched: Shuai Guo · math.AG, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We study the closed and open Gromov--Witten potentials of the toric Calabi--Yau threefold $$ X_p=\operatorname{Tot}\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(p-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-p-1)\bigr),\qquad p\geq 2. $$ We prove closed and open mirror symmetry under a nonvanishing condition on the torus weights, relating these potentials to topological recursion on the mirror curves. We establish polynomial structures for both the higher-genus closed potentials and the stable open potentials. We also establish double-scaling limits for topological recursion on the mirror curves. In particular, our results for the closed potentials prove the higher-genus ansatz and the double-scaling conjecture of Caporaso--Griguolo--Mari\~no--Pasquetti--Seminara.

PDF

item.title: Stable ample vector bundles without semipositive Kobayashi curvature
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan

Matched: Kefeng Liu · math.DG, math.CV · new

We construct slope-stable ample rank-two vector bundles on every Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb{F}_e$ that admit no smooth strongly pseudoconvex Finsler metric with semipositive Kobayashi curvature. These examples give a negative answer to Kobayashi's problem. The same bundles give counterexamples to the smooth strongly pseudoconvex Finsler formulation of Fulton's problem and to the Hartshorne--Schneider conjecture on the convexity of complements. For $e=1$, these counterexamples have a simply connected Fano base that is not a product.

item.title: From $3$-spin to Negative $r$-spin: Limits of Cohomological Field Theories and Tautological Relations
item.author: Deniz Genlik, Felix Janda
item.description:
Deniz Genlik, Felix Janda

Matched: Felix Janda · math.AG, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We prove that the negative $r$-spin tautological relations of Chidambaram--Garcia-Failde--Giacchetto are a consequence of Pixton's $3$-spin relations, for every $r\ge2$, and deduce that they hold in the tautological Chow ring of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$. In particular, our result for $r=2$ implies that Kazarian--Norbury $K$-relations hold in Chow. The proof factors through two essential parts. The first part shows that the tautological relations arising from Chiodo's class imply the negative $r$-spin relations. This requires an intricate study of limiting behavior of the Givental--Teleman graph contributions. In the second part, we show that the Chiodo relations are a consequence of Pixton's $3$-spin relations as an application of a generalization of Janda's work on tautological relations from CohFTs.
